newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ share market ends lacklustre session lower.
newsitem.headline: NZ share market ends lacklustre session lower.

text.p: * NZ share market ends weaker after lacklustre session
* Telecom edges lower, Fletcher Paper well sought
329 nil * NZSC cap index -19.93 at 5119.70 292 +3 * NZSE-10 cap index -2.13 at 1,156.92 359 -4 * Volume NZ$43 million. Futures +1 at 1,165
The New Zealand share market finished a lacklustre session on Thursday slightly weaker and brokers expect the flat trend to continue with a downward bias.
The death of Chinese paramount leader Deng Xiaoping left the market completely unmoved.
The top 40 index ended 3.5 points lower at 2325.85 on light total volume of $43 million.
Telecom's lacklustre third quarter performance remains a drag on the market and its two cent fall to $6.85 again made it hard for the share index to gain forward momentum.

Fletcher Paper rose three cents to $2.92, with investors expecting newsprint prices to respond positively to merger activity in North America. However, fellow forester Carter Holt Harvey was unmoved on $3.29.
Fletcher Energy closed just one cent ahead at $4.00 after reporting "encouraging progress" at two of its wells.
Brierley Investments recovered from morning weakness to end at $1.36 and hold Wednesday's gains.
Waste Management, one of the stellar performers of 1996, fell back 15 cents to $5.70 after reporting a flat year profit of $7.5 million.
